title: fix(plugin-form): opening a collapsed section keeps focus on its header the first time (objectui#13246)
body:
Fixes #13246

Clause-②: no

## What changed

`ModalForm` and `DrawerForm` now open and close a form section as a React transition: `startTransition` around the toggle's `setCollapsedSections`, through one local `setSectionCollapsed` per form, used by both of each form's section pushes. Nothing else moves: no export, prop, schema key or type member. `SectionDivider`'s keyboard handling (objectui#13220) is untouched, and nothing under `packages/components/src/ui/**` is edited.

## Why: the mechanism, measured

The card's mechanism assumption 2 holds with one correction: the header is **hidden**, not unmounted. The toggle was an ordinary update; the newly drawn `React.lazy` widget suspended; the nearest boundary that already showed content took the suspension, and React set `display: none` on what it had drawn, keeping it mounted. Measured in a unit test on unfixed `main` (`e70c21d`, which carries `4b92c5a`):

| host | mid-load | header rendered mid-load | focus mid-load | focus after load | next Tab |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ModalForm | `modal-form-body-pending` shown | no (ancestor `display: none`) | body | the `role="dialog"` element | `title`, the dialog's first field |
| DrawerForm | the HOST's fallback shown (the drawer has no boundary of its own) | no | body | an input, not the header | not the group's field |
| ObjectForm `simple` (probe only, not changed here) | the host's fallback shown | no | body | body | not read |

The modal row is the seat's live reading on the Semantic Zoo `money` group. The focus loss itself comes from the browser's focus fixup rule, which happy-dom lacks. Measured in headless Chromium (`/opt/pw-browsers/chromium`): a focused element whose ancestor is set to `display: none` keeps focus synchronously, loses it to the body by the next frame, and does not get it back when it is shown again. The new test restores that rule with a small MutationObserver (`emulateFocusFixup`), so it reads what the browser does; its "rendered" assertions read the mechanism with no emulation at all. In the dialog, Radix's focus scope then moves body focus to the dialog element when the fallback's nodes are removed, which is why the modal ends on `role="dialog"`.

`DrawerForm` was measured to share the shape, and worse: its toggle hid everything under the host's boundary, which is the objectui#12559 shape for the drawer. It gets the same treatment, per the claim's file surface.

## Route chosen, and why not a boundary per field

A transition that suspends at a boundary which already shows content keeps that content on screen until the new rows can be drawn. Measured in both hosts: the header is never hidden, keeps focus through the load, the group opens when its widget lands, and the next Tab reaches the group's first field.

The suggested alternative, a Suspense boundary around each lazily loaded field widget in the form renderer, was read and not taken:

- The widget is the single child of `FormControl`'s Slot, which hands `id` and `aria-*` to that child. A boundary there needs a forwarding wrapper around every registered widget.
- It changes every form's first draw, not only the toggle: rows would arrive one by one, and `useInitialFieldFocus` (objectui#13130, objectui#13219) could settle on the second field while the first is still loading.
- The card is about the toggle. The transition fixes it in the two hosts that own the toggle state, and leaves the dialog's body boundary owning every other wait.

The cost of this route, said plainly: during the load the section still shows collapsed. It opens when its rows can be drawn, with no placeholder in that window.

## The objectui#12559 pins: one line changed, one case added

Mechanism assumption 3 ("its pins must stay green") does not hold for one line. The first case asserted that mid-load the dialog body shows `modal-form-body-pending`. That placeholder replacing the body is exactly what hid the focused header, so no change that keeps focus can keep that line. It now asserts that the body stays drawn: no body placeholder, and the typed `first_name` input is not under `display: none`. Every other assertion of that case (no host fallback, no remount, one schema read, the typed value kept, the section open after load) is unchanged, and the other three cases are untouched.

Because the toggle no longer reaches the body boundary, that case stopped exercising it. A new case pins the boundary on an ordinary update, the body's first draw after the load with the deferred widget in an open section: the dialog shows its own placeholder and the host's fallback never mounts.

## Tests

- New: `packages/plugin-form/src/__tests__/sectionOpenKeepsFocus-13246.test.tsx`. For each host (modal, drawer): the first opening by Enter with the widget unresolved keeps the header rendered and focused mid-load, with no host fallback; after the load the group is open, focus is still on the header, and Tab reaches the group's widget. A control per host: once the chunk is loaded, Space closes and Enter reopens with focus on the header. The controls are green on unfixed `main` too, so the focus emulation does not produce a false red.
- On unfixed `main` (`e70c21d`): 2 failed (the modal and drawer first openings, at "header rendered"), 2 passed (the controls).
- On this branch: 4 of 4; together with the objectui#12559 file, 9 of 9.

## Ablation (head `583c45f`, through `ablation-replace.mjs`; each restore proven by blob equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`)

- `ModalForm`'s `startTransition` removed: red on the modal first-opening case and the objectui#12559 header-click case; 7 others green.
- `DrawerForm`'s `startTransition` removed: red on the drawer first-opening case only; 3 others green.
- Coverage proof of the new objectui#12559 case: `ModalForm`'s body Suspense boundary removed: red on the new "first draw waits inside the dialog" case only; 4 others green. A first attempt at this one was refused by the tool before it ran anything (its replacement text already occurred inside the anchor), and was re-run with a distinct replacement.

## Gates (head `583c45f`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-form/`: 198 files, 2372 passed, 1 skipped, exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form type-check` (echoes `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form lint`: 0 errors, exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `pnpm check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `pnpm check:control-bytes`, `pnpm check:changeset-claims`, `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals`, `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: each exit 0.
- Repo-wide lint and the full test farm are CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- `ObjectForm`'s full-page form (`formType: 'simple'`) has the same toggle path: a unit probe on this branch shows the host's fallback replacing the page and focus ending on the body. It is outside this claim's file surface and is not changed. No real producer was found: no app under objectstack `examples/` declares `editMode`, which is what routes the console to its full-page form. Carrier: none.
- Every arm builds its toggle through `resolveSectionCollapse` (`fieldGroups.ts`), so one `startTransition` there would cover every arm, `ObjectForm` included. Not done here: outside the file surface.
- Read from source only, not measured: a `visibleWhen` that reveals a field whose widget is not loaded yet is still an ordinary update, so it would still hide the dialog body behind its placeholder.
